I have the right to question him relating to this signed comment. Now, he might want to come up and say to basically protect himself against conviction to come up and say this is a false statement. Obviously he's admitted to all sorts of criminal actions, surely he's going to say it's a false statement, but I have the right to confront this witness with the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Weiner. Because according to -- as Mr. Pantelic has pointed out, the accused Blagoje Simic was contesting the contents of this statement. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On the second day, but not on the first day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. But the fact that is that it is being contested by the accused and no finding has been made whether or not it was voluntary at this stage, so it may not be proper to put the contents of that statement to any witness. Because the issue whether or not that statement was voluntary, whether or not he read it, he understood it, before he signed it, and whether or not it is in fact his statement has yet to be decided upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, aren't I entitled to confront him and ask him if it's true? What if he then says, "It is true. That did in fact happen"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You may ask it as a general -- as an ordinary question, but not as a statement made by Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue on that statement. Sir, isn't it true that the War Presidency was involved in inviting Crni and the volunteers from Serbia back to Bosanski Samac after they had left the area in the beginning of the summer? After they had left in the beginning of the summer, isn't it true that the War Presidency had invited them back?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Presidency did not fill the military units, because how is it possible that the War Presidency calls up somebody and suggests to the military structures to take those people under their command? This is impossible. The War Presidency did not call up any citizens from any area in order to fill up the military ranks. That was not one of its duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, will you look at the third paragraph on that same page, the third sentence. I'll read it. "Crni arrived for the second time on the invitation of the Samac Municipal War Presidency and with the approval of the command and Colonel Novica Simic. I'd like to stress that no reward was offered to him for coming to the Posavina front." Words illegible after that. "Under the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, you should the command of" -- then it's illegible,"who appointed him commander of the assault battalion earn" illegible. "Crni asked to bring volunteers from Serbia and Colonel Simic and Major Beronja enabled him to do so, after which approximately," another illegible, "volunteers arrived from Kragujevac, although a higher number had been mentioned prior to that." And then the last sentence of this page. "Debeli was offered -- in fact, he requested that we enable him to carry out Orasje war booty in the amount of 50.000 D-mark. Did I read both of those correctly, both of those statements correctly?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that there is complete confusion in the information here for me, so that I admit that I am not able to find my way around all this information. I don't know why Crni was to have been called from Serbia, when it is well known that he was married to a woman from Samac, Lizja Jusufovic [phoen]. Also, I don't know why Debeli was to have been called when he is marry to a woman from Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten her --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Didn't I read both of those statements correctly? Didn't I read both of those correctly?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did read it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question is: Do you agree that the War Presidency invited the Serbian volunteers back for a second time to Bosanski Samac? You might agree. Do you agree with that statement of Blagoje Simic -- or alleged statement of Blagoje Simic or not?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not understanding that from this text, you read this correctly. But you said that Crni was being invited then volunteers and then General Simic and Beronja were also being called, who are officers of Republika Srpska. So this is a kind of semantic confusion and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. All right, sir. Why don't you look at the -- at document -- P127. Maybe states it a little bit better. And that document actually was written prior to this statement. Why don't we look at that, page 4. Do you still very well that document, the 12 signatories? Yes. Could you look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is this, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 4. Look for the ninth paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. First on page 4, the ninth paragraph, if we read, beginning with the third sentence. "The civilian authorities instructed by the Presidency and some government members decided to engage the volunteers from Serbia initially under the control of Debeli, but this command was taken over by Crni in the arrival phase. The decision also set the fee for fighting the war. Allegedly at D-mark 50.000 per man, provided they conquered Orasje, and ample war booty was found there. Crni promised to bring in more than 700 volunteers, but about 300 arrived in the first round. In fact, only 30 volunteers, some of whom had never seen a battlefield." Did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You read it correctly. Again, this is a set-up with a lot of imagination. This is well known from rigged trials of a Stalinist nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 5, the second -- or the third full paragraph, in the middle. "Why did someone try to bring Crni and his people back at any cost, though people knew what had happened to him and those like him during the first arrest and how he had in fact discredited himself as a person and the post he had held? Why were there requests for the return of Lugar, the man who had not only committed a war crime but had together with like minds forced a legacy of fear and war on our Serbian people and our Serbian fighters in this region?" Again, they talk about bringing this group back. Do you agree that this document indicates that the War Presidency invited this group back from Serbia, Crni, Debeli, and his friends? Do you agree the document indicates that, they read it correctly, that that's what this document indicates? That's the first question.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the document, but of course this is incorrect. Somebody from the command of the brigade is stating that he brought into his ranks Lugar and Crni yet again. Who is this being stated to? I don't know. And all of this is after military investigative prison at that, so people were at a military investigative prison and then they went elsewhere and then they were brought to the military structures again and now somebody is asking the Crisis Staff how come these people are here. That is something that no one from the Crisis Staff could have known, or I am not aware of anybody having known about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know any reason why this document, these 13 military officers, would indicate that the War Presidency brought Crni back, which is consistent with Blagoje Simic's own admissions -- own alleged admissions that the War Presidency brought them back, if it wasn't true, sir? Do you know of any reason?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this is even alleged admission, I would like to know where and when this alleged admission was made. I mean, fairly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In Exhibit 116, the alleged admission that we just read a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The statement which the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The alleged statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Which the accused --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is consistent with the alleged statement. And my question to is him does he know of any reason --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which is fully contested by --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's the alleged statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Weiner. You are confusing the witness. Just withdraw that question. Reorganise it and put evidence which is unlike the contested statement of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know of any reason why the -- why Simo Zaric and these 12 other military officers would indicate that the War Presidency was involved in bringing back Crni, Lugar, and the volunteers from Serbia? And this is at a period after the Crkvina massacre. Why they brought the -- why the War Presidency would bring these people back if it wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of the return of volunteers is their matter. It is not something for the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. My question is -- whether you want to use the phrase "Crisis Staff" or "War Presidency," are you aware of any reason why these people would make this statement, 13 military officers have signed this statement indicating that the War Presidency was involved in bringing these people back, Crni, Lugar, Debeli, and this is at a period after the Crkvina massacre by some of these people -- why they would bring these people back if it wasn't true. Why would they make that statement?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this document has to do with the military structures, and it was not made public, then the reasons are something that I am not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were a member of the War Presidency, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And that's precisely why I am asking why within the military the investigative organs, the prosecutor, the court, everybody, did not arrest these people if they had such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question is -- my question is: Were you a member of the War Presidency? Were you a member?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you a member after that of the Samac Municipal Assembly in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you a member throughout the year 1993?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the year 1993 until the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, isn't it true that the Municipal Assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Samac awarded Vidovdan/St. Vitus Day decorations to a group of soldiers, including Milan Josic [phoen], Milos Bogdanovic posthumously, Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni, and Srecko Radovanovic, also known as Debeli? Isn't it true that these people were arrested decorations for the successful command and control of units of the Army of the Republika Srpska, the defence of the people in Serbian land? Isn't that true that they were awarded those decorations, sir, in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we get to the same thing. The members of the municipal assembly did not make any proposals from their own heads, so to speak, or did they explain certain --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question was: Were those individuals awarded decorations, St. Vidovdan decorations for --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the proposal of the military, yes. Officers, that is. And people from the civilian authorities were awarded on the basis of proposals made by the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, these decorations were awarded, and it indicates the signature of Dr. Blagoje Simic, and it talks about decision to award -- and this is a decision of the Serbian Municipality, and they adopted a decision to award this. Not the military; the Serbian Municipal Assembly adopted a decision to award Crni and Debeli decorations for the successful command and control of units of the Army of the Republika Srpska. Would you like to see it in Exhibit P126A, or can you tell us were those people awarded decorations?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe it would be fair for the witness to have this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let him see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And for the defendants. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let him look at the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: P126 is the Bosnian. P126A, I believe, is the English -- the English translation of that particular portion. In B/C/S, it's item 35 on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The marking on the top is 00456650. You'll see a group of markings on the top of each page. 456650. Do you see the award?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page? Which number -- which page number and which issue of the Official Gazette, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, right. I think I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see item 35, in the right column?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It says --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "Pursuant" -- and it indicates a session on June 24th, 1993 -- "of the Samac Municipal Assembly adopted a decision to award Vidovdan/St. Vitus Day decorations." In Article 2: "Decorations shall be awarded to the following for the successful command and control of the units of the Army of Republika Srpska, the defence of the people, and Serbian land." And the last two there of the four people named: "Dragan Djordjevic, Crni; and Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli." Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the decision it says that this recognition is bestowed on all fallen soldiers, all commanders of battalions. Yes, all commanders of battalions. Djordjevic was one of the commanders and I assume --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you awarded Crni and Debeli a Vidovdan award or Vidovdan decoration for successful command and control of their units even though it was their volunteer unit that committed the Crkvina massacre.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, none of these persons committed the massacre in Crkvina, none of those who were given these awards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think it's about time for our adjournment. But maybe my learned friend can clarify it. Who do you think "we" -- I mean, "you," you as Mr. Simic, Simeon or you and -- in extended. Could you clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The municipal assembly awarded these people Vidovdan decorations for the successful command and control of units of the Army of the Republika Srpska, even though the unit that they commanded and controlled committed the Crkvina massacre against the -- against 16 -- by killing 16 non-Serb civilians. The fact that their units committed a massacre, is that successful command and control? Is that how the Serbian assembly found that to be successful command and control?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the assembly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- My learned friend. I mean, could you divide it for the witness. What is the question? The fact that they allegedly committed a massacre? Who -- and then how the Serbian assembly found that -- I agree. You can ask whatever you think, which is necessary for your case, but still in fairness to the witness, I think the question should be split or divided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we adjourn. We're running out of tape. We'll adjourn the proceedings and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: at 4.19 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of December, 2002, at 9.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
